subject: Biology
title: Molecular Mechanisms of Hormone Action: GPCR vs. Nuclear Receptors
learningObjectives: Trace the Adenylate Cyclase-cAMP-PKA signal transduction cascade
Describe the Phospholipase C (PLC) IP3/DAG and Ca2+-Calmodulin pathway
Detail how lipid-soluble hormone-receptor complexes bind Hormone Response Elements (HRE) on DNA
content:
Hormones trigger physiological responses in target tissues by binding specific protein Hormone Receptors.

```
                        HORMONE RECEPTOR MECHANISMS
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
  MEMBRANE-BOUND RECEPTORS                                INTRACELLULAR / NUCLEAR RECEPTORS
  (Water-Soluble: Peptides & Catecholamines)              (Lipid-Soluble: Steroids & T₃/T₄)
  ├── Cannot cross lipid bilayer                          ├── Diffuses directly across plasma membrane
  ├── Generates Second Messengers                         ├── Binds nuclear receptor to form Hormone-
  │   (cAMP, IP₃, DAG, Ca²⁺)                              │   Receptor Complex
  └── Activates Protein Kinases (PKA / PKC)               └── Binds DNA HRE to regulate Transcription
```

### 2.1 Second Messenger Signal Transduction Cascades

```
                     GPCR-cAMP SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION CASCADES
                     
   Water-Soluble Hormone (1st Messenger) ──► Binds Cell-Surface GPCR Receptor
                                                     │
   Activates Transmembrane Adenylate Cyclase ◄───────┘
               │
   Converts ATP ──► Cyclic AMP (cAMP) (2nd Messenger)
                           │
   Activates Protein Kinase A (PKA) ──► Phosphorylates Target Proteins ──► Physiological Response
```

```
                     PLC-IP₃ / DAG SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION CASCADES
                     
   Hormone ──► GPCR ──► Activates Phospholipase C (PLC) ──► Cleaves PIP₂ into IP₃ + DAG
                                                                   │
   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┐
   ▼                                                                                               ▼
   IP₃ triggers Ca²⁺ release from ER lumen                                                         DAG activates Protein
   Ca²⁺ binds Calmodulin ──► Downstream Kinase Activation                                          Kinase C (PKC)
```

### 2.2 Gene Expression Regulation by Nuclear Receptors

```
                   INTRACELLULAR / NUCLEAR RECEPTOR CASCADE
                   
   Lipid-Soluble Hormone (Steroid/T₃) ──► Diffuses across lipid bilayer into Cytosol / Nucleus
                                                    │
   Binds Intracellular Receptor ──► Forms Hormone-Receptor Complex
                                                    │
   Translocates to Nucleus ──► Binds Hormone Response Element (HRE) on DNA
                                                    │
   Alters mRNA Transcription ──► Protein Translation ──► Physiological Response
```

conceptBreakdown.heading: Amplification Cascade of Second Messengers
conceptBreakdown.explanation: A single hormone molecule binding to a GPCR can activate multiple G-proteins, generating thousands of cAMP molecules and activating numerous PKA enzymes to phosphorylate millions of substrate proteins within seconds.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Zinc Finger Motifs in Nuclear Receptors
conceptBreakdown.explanation: Intracellular nuclear hormone receptors possess a central DNA-binding domain containing conserved Zinc Finger motifs that recognize specific palindromic or direct-repeat nucleotide sequences in Hormone Response Elements (HREs).
